Why the same costs can sink one strategy and barely touch another 📉

Spread, commission and slippage are charged on every trade, win or lose. With fixed-risk sizing, a tighter stop means a bigger position, so it pays more of them.

In our (hypothetical) simulation, one strategy with a +0.125R edge per trade before costs paid 1.5 pips per round trip. With a 50-pip stop, 6% of runs lost money. With a 5-pip stop, 99.9% did.

New on the blog:
• how to measure costs in R instead of pips
• what costs do to expectancy, breakeven win rate and profit factor
• what research on real investors and published strategies found about costs and turnover
• why spreads and slippage are not constant
• a checklist for pricing costs into a backtest
